# Purpose

This solver estimates one elevation per point from measured height differences between pairs of points. It follows Condit's equal-weight least-squares calculation.

Such records can come from establishing a plot grid. A team marks points with stakes and measures the vertical difference between pairs, for example by levelling with an instrument and a graduated staff. The coordinates may also describe other surveyed locations. The solver works on irregularly spaced points and does not require a complete regular grid. [Condit's survey example](https://ctfs.si.edu/Public/CTFSRPackage/files/tutorials/topography/)

This is a limited tool for pairwise survey records. For a new survey, professional instruments or drone mapping may provide a more detailed elevation model with less manual processing. Drone products can include vegetation, so confirm that the product represents the ground surface. [USGS drone elevation products](https://www.usgs.gov/centers/eros/science/usgs-eros-archive-unmanned-aircraft-systems-uas-dems)

# Read the survey and estimate elevations

The supplied CSV is simulated. It contains 49 points on a 30 by 30 m plot, with repeated measurements, small disagreements and mixed measurement directions. All coordinates and differences are in metres. Change the paths and reference parameters for your survey.

The default paths below work when rendering this tutorial or running from the repository root. Set a full path to fgeo2 when using the code elsewhere.

```{r}
#| label: read-survey

# install.packages(c("Matrix", "igraph", "jsonlite"))
path.to.fgeo2 = if(file.exists("../../fgeo2.Rproj")) "../.." else "."
# path.to.fgeo2 = "/full/path/to/fgeo2"

# Assign this elevation to the point at these coordinates.
reference.xy = c(0, 0)
reference.z = 100  # Use 0 for relative elevations if absolute elevation is unknown.

source(file.path(path.to.fgeo2, "06_topography_habitat/R/new/topography-solver.R"))
records <- read.csv(file.path(path.to.fgeo2, "data_examples/topography-survey.csv"))

# One row per measured difference. Positive dz means the destination is higher.
survey <- data.frame(
	x_i = records$from_x_m,
	y_i = records$from_y_m,
	x_j = records$to_x_m,
	y_j = records$to_y_m,
	dz = records$height_difference_m
)

elevations <- estimate_point_elevations(survey, reference.xy, reference.z)
head(elevations)
```

Other file layouts must be processed into the same five-column `survey` table. The solver identifies points by exact coordinate pairs, so use consistent coordinates for repeated points. The point IDs in this example file are only used by the old solver below.

Rows and columns can be in any order. Repeated and conflicting measurements receive equal weight. Incomplete rows are omitted with a warning. Missing measurements or missing grid points are acceptable while the remaining observations connect every retained point. Points represented only by omitted rows disappear from the output. The result contains `x`, `y` and `z`; raster construction and interpolation are separate steps.

# Compare with Condit's solver

The old code is read from fgeo2 as it stood through 2026-11-09 (UTC), before this replacement. This avoids depending on copies in the current `R/old` or `evaluation/Condit` folders. The date lookup needs internet access and `jsonlite`.

```{r}
#| label: load-old-solver

source(file.path(path.to.fgeo2, "evaluation/0-code-to-source.r"))
old <- new.env()
load_github_snapshot(
	commit.date = "2026-11-09",
	scripts = "06_topography_habitat/R/new/topography-solvetopo.r",
	envir = old
)

# If needed, replace the call above with ONE alternative below.
# source(file.path(path.to.fgeo2, "06_topography_habitat/R/old/topography-solvetopo.r"), local = old)
# source(file.path(path.to.fgeo2, "evaluation/Condit/topography/solvetopo.r"), local = old)
# old$solve.topo <- ctfs::solve_topo  # Requires the ctfs package.
```

First compare relative elevations at datum zero. Both solvers should reconcile the measurements in the same way.

```{r}
#| label: compare-elevations

# Condit's solver needs point IDs and a coordinate lookup.
points <- unique(rbind(
	data.frame(id = records$from_point, x = records$from_x_m, y = records$from_y_m),
	data.frame(id = records$to_point, x = records$to_x_m, y = records$to_y_m)
))
points <- points[order(points$x, points$y), ]
base.id <- points$id[points$x == reference.xy[1] & points$y == reference.xy[2]]

old.survey <- data.frame(
	pt1 = records$from_point,
	pt2 = records$to_point,
	htdiff = records$height_difference_m
)
old.fit <- old$solve.topo(old.survey, basept = base.id, baseelev = 0)
old.z <- old.fit$elev[match(points$id, old.fit$label)]
new.fit <- estimate_point_elevations(survey, reference.xy, reference.z = 0)

# Align by coordinates, then check agreement.
stopifnot(all(points$x == new.fit$x), all(points$y == new.fit$y))
max(abs(old.z - new.fit$z))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(old.z, new.fit$z, tolerance = 1e-8)))
```

The two panels show the same fitted terrain. `persp()` uses a rectangular grid for this display; the solver itself also accepts irregular point networks. Both panels use the same scales and viewing angles. [R perspective plots](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/graphics/html/persp.html)

```{r}
#| label: fig-terrain-comparison
#| fig-cap: "Relative elevations from the same survey. Condit's solver and the new solver agree."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4

x <- sort(unique(new.fit$x))
y <- sort(unique(new.fit$y))
old.surface <- new.surface <- matrix(NA_real_, length(x), length(y))

# Matrix rows correspond to x and columns to y.
old.surface[cbind(match(points$x, x), match(points$y, y))] <- old.z
new.surface[cbind(match(new.fit$x, x), match(new.fit$y, y))] <- new.fit$z
z.limits <- range(old.z, new.fit$z)

settings <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1))
persp(x, y, old.surface, zlim = z.limits, theta = 35, phi = 25,
      scale = FALSE, col = "lightblue", shade = 0.4,
      xlab = "x (m)", ylab = "y (m)", zlab = "z (m)", main = "Condit")
persp(x, y, new.surface, zlim = z.limits, theta = 35, phi = 25,
      scale = FALSE, col = "lightblue", shade = 0.4,
      xlab = "x (m)", ylab = "y (m)", zlab = "z (m)", main = "New solver")
par(settings)
```

# Small checks for the old problems

A chain with differences of 2 and 3 m should give elevations 100, 102 and 105 m when its first point is at 100 m. The old code applies the datum only to the first point. It also mishandles reordered columns and propagates a missing difference. These small examples show the fixes.

```{r}
#| label: check-old-problems

chain <- data.frame(x_i = c(0, 1), y_i = 0, x_j = c(1, 2), y_j = 0, dz = c(2, 3))
old.chain <- data.frame(pt1 = c("1", "2"), pt2 = c("2", "3"), htdiff = c(2, 3))

# A nonzero datum must shift every point.
rbind(
	Condit = old$solve.topo(old.chain, baseelev = 100)$elev,
	New = estimate_point_elevations(chain, reference.z = 100)$z
)

# Reordering columns must preserve the direction of the measured differences.
rbind(
	Condit = old$solve.topo(old.chain[c("pt2", "pt1", "htdiff")])$elev,
	New = estimate_point_elevations(chain[c("dz", "x_j", "y_j", "x_i", "y_i")])$z
)

# An extra row with a missing difference must not contaminate usable measurements.
rbind(
	Condit = old$solve.topo(rbind(old.chain, transform(old.chain[1, ], htdiff = NA)))$elev,
	New = estimate_point_elevations(rbind(chain, transform(chain[1, ], dz = NA)))$z
)

stopifnot(
	isTRUE(all.equal(estimate_point_elevations(chain, reference.z = 100)$z, c(100, 102, 105))),
	isTRUE(all.equal(estimate_point_elevations(chain[2:1, 5:1])$z, c(0, 2, 5)))
)
```
